blogs.title: Scaling React Apps Without the Pain
blogs.excerpt: Patterns for structure, state management, and performance as your app grows.
blogs.content:
As React applications grow in complexity, maintaining a clean and scalable architecture becomes crucial. In this post, we'll explore proven patterns for structuring large React codebases.

Project Structure

A well-organized folder structure is the foundation of any scalable app. Consider organizing by feature rather than by type.

State Management

Choose your state management solution wisely. For most applications, a combination of React Context and local state works well.

Performance Optimization

Use React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback strategically. Profile your app before optimizing.
blogs.author: Alex Morgan

blogs.title: A Practical Guide to Multi-Tenant SaaS
blogs.excerpt: Trade-offs, data isolation strategies, and operational considerations.
blogs.content:
Building multi-tenant SaaS applications requires careful consideration of data isolation, security, and scalability.

Tenant Isolation Strategies

There are three main approaches: database-per-tenant, schema-per-tenant, and shared tables with tenant IDs.

Security Considerations

Always validate tenant context at the API layer. Never trust client-side tenant identifiers.

Operational Excellence

Implement proper monitoring and alerting per tenant to catch issues early.
blogs.author: Alex Morgan

blogs.title: Observability Basics for Product Teams
blogs.excerpt: How to ship features faster with logs, metrics, and traces.
blogs.content:
Observability is not just for ops teams. Product engineers benefit immensely from understanding how their code behaves in production.

The Three Pillars

Logs, metrics, and traces form the foundation of observability. Each serves a different purpose.

Getting Started

Start with structured logging. Use correlation IDs to trace requests across services.

Actionable Alerts

Set up alerts that lead to action. Avoid alert fatigue by being selective.
